provider.name: Notion
provider.identityReason: Notion is a workspace productivity and database platform at notion.so with official OAuth and API for third-party integrations.

managedOption.details: Composio lists Notion as an available integration, but the exact OAuth delegation method (managed vs. direct) is not documented on Composio's public pages.

setup: Confirmed: Register your integration at https://www.notion.so/my-integrations to receive Client ID and Client Secret.
Confirmed: Notion OAuth endpoints are at https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize (authorization) and https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token (token exchange).
Confirmed: Set one or more Redirect URIs during app registration; Notion requires exact URI match (no wildcards).
Confirmed: OAuth flow is server-side (Authorization Code) with PKCE support optional but recommended.
Confirmed: During authorization, users grant your app access to specified pages and databases; access is not workspace-wide by default.
scopeFindings: Confirmed: Notion uses capabilities-based permissions, not traditional OAuth scopes. Capabilities are configured per integration in the integration settings.
Confirmed: Available capabilities include read content, update content, insert content, and delete content at the page/database level.
Confirmed: Integrations request access to specific pages/databases; users explicitly grant access during the OAuth consent flow.
Confirmed: No pre-defined scope list exists; permissions are object-specific. Documentation at https://developers.notion.com/reference/capabilities describes integration permissions.
Estimate: A typical multi-user AI agent will need read and update capabilities on user-selected pages and databases.
testAndLaunch: Confirmed: Test mode is not required. Developer can create a test integration and connect it to a personal or test workspace immediately after registration.
Confirmed: No sandbox environment exists; testing occurs directly in Notion with real workspaces.
Confirmed: Integrations begin in 'internal' mode (accessible only to the workspace owner) until submitted for public distribution.

Confirmed: To make your integration public, submit it for review via https://www.notion.so/my-integrations; review includes verification that the integration follows Notion API guidelines and security practices.
Unknown: Estimated review time for public distribution is not published by Notion.
review: Confirmed: Public integrations require submission and approval via Notion's integration review process.
Confirmed: Review criteria include proper OAuth implementation, correct permission handling, compliance with Terms of Service, and security (no hardcoded secrets, secure token storage).
Confirmed: Notion's review team may request changes or rejections if the integration misuses data or violates guidelines.
Unknown: No published SLA or estimated turnaround for review decisions.
support: Confirmed: Official developer documentation is at https://developers.notion.com with API reference, OAuth guide, and capability details.
Confirmed: Notion offers a community Slack workspace for developer support and questions.
Confirmed: Official support for integrations and OAuth issues is available through Notion's Help Center and developer forum.
Confirmed: Notion publishes a changelog and deprecation notices at https://developers.notion.com/changelog for API updates.
result.nextAction: Register your integration at https://www.notion.so/my-integrations, configure the Redirect URI (e.g., https://yourdomain.com/oauth/callback), retrieve your Client ID and Secret, then implement the Authorization Code flow using Notion's OAuth endpoints. Test with a personal workspace before submitting for public review. Verify whether Composio's managed OAuth option handles Notion token refresh and permission mapping.

result.difficultyReason: Notion OAuth setup is straightforward (standard Authorization Code flow), but the capabilities-based permission model differs from traditional scopes, requiring careful configuration to avoid over-requesting access. Public review adds a compliance step. Composio's managed option may hide complexity.
result.handsOnEffort: 2–4 hours to set up OAuth, test with a workspace, and prepare for public submission; 1–2 additional hours if changes are requested during review.
result.approvalWait: Unknown: Notion does not publish review turnaround time.
result.biggestBlocker: No published SLA for public integration review; blocking approval time is uncertain.
